solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disease comes from shops getting in special beef

indicators.note: the shopping centre gets in between the other pieces, sitting inside them

parts.note: a mall is a place full of shops
an ox is a beef animal

explanation.surface: A warning that eating specially sourced beef bought at the shops could make you ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' is the container signal; 'shops' stands for one shopping centre rather than many stores.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallpox is a highly contagious viral illness, now eradicated, so it is an example of a disease.

clue.text: Strict clergyman back in religious office

indicators.note: the clergyman's title goes in the bishop's seat

parts.note: a see is a bishop's office or diocese

indicators.note: back means the clergyman's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A stern priest returns to the church office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal and 'in' the container; a see is a bishop's seat, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh and stern, the same as strict.

clue.text: Risky having gold card right away, running up debts

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: in a down entry, running up means the word is written upwards
away tells us the right letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: Using a gold credit card recklessly, piling up debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' takes R from CARD to leave CAD, and 'running up' turns it to DAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacious means daring and bold, prepared to take risks.

clue.text: Made yard cleaner, particularly floor?

indicators.note: particularly can mean peculiarly or unusually, so the letters come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: Tidying the yard thoroughly, especially the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'particularly' is the anagram signal, in its sense of peculiarly. A dance floor gives the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to baffle them, and leading them a merry dance confuses and frustrates them.

clue.text: One into globe-trotting, finally homeward bound

indicators.note: the numeral goes into the rearranged letters
globe-trotting suggests the letters travel about and are mixed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of homeward

explanation.surface: A world traveller finally heads home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trotting' turns GLOBE into OBLGE; 'into' puts I inside to give OBLIGE; 'finally' adds D.
explanation.definitionFit: Obliged means under obligation, duty-bound to do something.

clue.text: Succulent ham, during course, systematically chopped

indicators.note: the acting word goes during, i.e. inside, the letters picked from the other word
cutting the word course at regular intervals leaves every other letter

parts.note: to ham is to act in an exaggerated way

explanation.surface: A chef serves a juicy ham, carved up methodically, as part of a meal course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'systematically chopped' keeps C, U, S from COURSE; 'during' puts ACT inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cactus is a classic succulent plant, storing water in its fleshy stems.

clue.text: An Arctic plunge that cuts no ice?

definitions.text: An Arctic plunge that cuts no ice?

parts.words: An Arctic plunge that cuts no ice?
parts.note: a dip into polar water read literally, and a phrase for something too small to make any difference

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a tiny amount with no real effect, which is what cutting no ice implies.

clue.text: Earth shifts for three in that location

indicators.note: the earth letter shifts to a new place in the number word

explanation.surface: The planet's crust shifts, displacing three things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' moves one E in THREE to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at that place, pointing somewhere away from the speaker.

clue.text: Visionary governing master set to alter academic period

indicators.note: governing means holding control round the other letters, containing them

parts.note: a seer is a visionary prophet

indicators.note: set to alter means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A far-sighted college head decides to change the term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to alter' is the anagram signal and 'governing' the container, as a ruler holds what it governs.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is half of an academic year, a teaching term.

clue.text: Inactive snake requires shelter

indicators.note: the snake takes in the shelter word, holding it inside

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: A dormant snake needs somewhere to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' acts as a container signal: the snake takes in what it needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is dormant and not active.

clue.text: Booze very shortly transformed party spirit

parts.note: very in short form is the abbreviation V

indicators.note: the two-letter party word is turned round, a small transformation of its order

parts.note: a do is a party
in Egyptian belief the ka is a person's spirit

explanation.surface: Drinking at a party quickly turns the mood into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' turns DO into OD. KA, the Egyptian notion of a spirit or soul, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a strong distilled drink, an example of booze.

clue.text: An East European, during meal, repositioned light

indicators.note: the people are placed during, i.e. inside, the rearranged meal
the letters of meal are moved around into new positions

parts.note: a Serb is a person from Serbia in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: Someone from Eastern Europe moves the lamp during dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repositioned' is the anagram signal and 'during' puts the people inside it; 'light' looks like an adjective but is the noun defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser beam is a narrow concentrated ray of light.

clue.text: Delivering destroyed fish box

indicators.note: delivering a speech means saying it, so the word is pronounced rather than written

parts.note: wrecked means destroyed
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: A ruined fish box is all that remains after a delivery goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivering' looks like a postal word but signals speech: WRECKED spoken gives RECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is the four-sided shape of a box drawn on paper, so box is a loose informal synonym.

clue.text: What button might say to get lift

definitions.meaning: a button is labelled with an instruction to push it
in weightlifting a ... is a lift pushing the weight overhead

explanation.surface: Instructions for summoning an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is printed on buttons as an order, and in weightlifting it names a type of lift.

clue.text: Up-market golf contest embraced by sides in tweed

indicators.note: the golf tournament is held inside the outer letters
the sides of the word tweed are its first and last letters

parts.note: the Open is a major golf championship

explanation.surface: A smart golfing event where everyone wears tweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides in' gives T and D from TWEED, and 'embraced by' puts OPEN between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-end goods are the most expensive, luxury range, which is what up-market describes.

clue.text: Window's broken by anonymous children. Dash!

indicators.note: the glass is broken open and other letters pushed into it

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of window glass

explanation.surface: Unknown kids smash a window and the onlooker curses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' signals the container. 'Dash!' looks like a mild curse but means flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash in the sense of stylish verve is a synonym for flamboyant flair.

clue.text: Bird makes tea very loundly, on edge

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loudly
to edge forward is to inch

explanation.surface: Making tea noisily while feeling nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loundly' is the printed typo for loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch, a bird.

clue.text: Walks organised with Deb becoming patchy

indicators.note: organised means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Arranged walks with a debutante turn out uneven.
explanation.walkthrough: SKEWBALD describes a horse with patches of white and another colour, not black.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewbald horse has irregular patches of white and brown, so it is patchy.

clue.text: Predator's hiding in Mike's trellis

indicators.note: the bird of prey is tucked inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A bird of prey lurks in a neighbour's garden trellis.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Predator stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kestrel is a small falcon that hunts, so it is a predator.

clue.text: Sheep and donkey trotted out for religious festival

indicators.note: trotted out means said or uttered, so these words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep and an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Farm animals are paraded at a church festival.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMMAS, 1 August, is an old English harvest festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Lammas is a Christian harvest festival held on 1 August.

clue.text: Some sweat covers pair of heretics seeing guillotine

indicators.note: the drop of sweat covers, i.e. surrounds, the other letters

parts.note: a bead is a small drop of sweat

indicators.note: a pair of the word's letters means its first two

explanation.surface: Heretics sweat nervously as they face the guillotine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of' takes the first two letters and 'covers' is the container signal; 'Some sweat' is a single drop of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To guillotine someone is to cut off their head, the verb meaning decapitate.

clue.text: School party northwards attracts curious sort

indicators.note: the party pulls the other letters into itself
in a down entry northwards means read upwards

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A political party courts an odd type of school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northwards' turns the party up the grid; 'curious' is the anagram signal; 'attracts' the container. A borstal was a British youth detention centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A borstal was a reform institution for young offenders, a kind of school.

clue.text: Dates transported around edge of Port Said

indicators.note: the date letters go around the picked letter
transported means moved about, so the letters are rearranged
the edge here is the final letter of Port

explanation.surface: Dates are shipped to the Egyptian port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' makes STAED from DATES, and 'around' puts T inside. 'Port Said' looks like the city; 'Said' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated is the past tense of state, meaning declared or said.

clue.text: Injury wrapped

definitions.meaning: a cut or gash in the body
past tense of wind, as thread round a spool

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a physical injury; as the past of wind it means coiled or wrapped round.

clue.text: Pure talk

definitions.meaning: complete or absolute, as in nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means sheer or absolute; as a verb it means to speak.

clue.text: Working farm contains terrace, volunteers turning over green veg

indicators.note: the rearranged farm letters hold the terrace word inside
working dough or clay reshapes it, so the farm letters are rearranged

parts.note: a row of terraced houses is a terrace

indicators.note: the volunteers' abbreviation is turned over, read the other way

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Farm hands and volunteers work the terrace to grow vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' is the anagram signal, 'contains' the container, 'turning over' the reversal. TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrowfat peas are a large variety of green pea, a vegetable.

clue.text: Sometime in the evening, Italian poet clipped page?

parts.note: at ten o'clock is a time in the evening

indicators.note: the poet's name is clipped short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: Reading a shortened page of Italian poetry late in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipped' cuts the final E from DANTE. The question mark flags that page here is a servant, not a sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a young servant who waits on someone, so a kind of attendant.

clue.text: Painter makes money? Not a jot, ultimately

indicators.note: not a means the letter a is left out

parts.note: to earn is to make money

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of jot

explanation.surface: An artist wonders whether painting pays, concluding it does not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a' removes A from EARNS, leaving ERNS; 'ultimately' adds T. Max Ernst was a German Surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a Dada and Surrealist artist, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Gateway reportedly established English county

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a door is a gateway into a room
set means established or fixed

explanation.surface: Locals say an old gateway was built in a rural county.
explanation.walkthrough: DORSET is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is a county in south-west England.

clue.text: College clock display, casing 25.4 mm, fastened securely

indicators.note: the display forms a case round the length measurement

parts.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode display used on digital clocks
one inch is 25.4 millimetres

explanation.surface: A college clock's display unit is mounted in a casing of exact size and bolted on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casing' is the container signal; 25.4 mm is the exact metric length of an inch.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a nail is to bend its point over so it holds tight, hence fastened firmly.
